title: Observation of Strong Phonon Anisotropy Across Dislocation Region in Oxide Freestanding Film
content: Vibrational electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) is a powerful STEM technique that has significantly advanced our understanding of phonon structure and thermal properties of materials at the atomic scale. By measuring the energy loss of electrons via interactions with materials, vibrational EELS provides detailed insights into the vibrational modes of atoms. This capability is crucial for studying the structural, chemical, and electronic properties of materials, especially at the nanoscale [1–5]. In this work, we employed the momentum-selective dark-field EELS approach to investigate the dislocation structure in barium titanate freestanding films and to examine the anisotropic response from the vibrational EELS signal.
